headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors from shared MCP/filesystem pathways; data leakage and compliance risks are also present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read/write runtime files and use MCP; Semantic Kernel can also use MCP and application-defined files. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one agent can be parsed by the other as instructions. The pathway is not proven by docs alone, so I avoid high, but it exists in default-capable pairings.
conditions: IF OpenHands writes untrusted content into a shared file or MCP payload that Semantic Kernel later reads as instructions
IF Semantic Kernel forwards MCP/tool output back into OpenHands without provenance filtering
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate workspaces
Disable MCP on one side for the first run
Add a provenance tag to every cross-agent message
Require manual review of any file passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenHands touches files mounted into its runtime and handles model-provider API keys; Semantic Kernel touches application context and can call external model providers and MCP servers. If they share a mounted volume or memory store, sensitive runtime files or context can flow from A into B and then out through B's API calls. The shared-data pathway is plausible from the profiles, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mounted volume or shared memory store
IF either agent sends retrieved file contents or application context to a third-party model API
mitigations: Use separate storage roots for each agent
Remove secrets from shared files before either agent runs
Turn off automatic context ingestion in Semantic Kernel
Limit OpenHands to a scratch directory only

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands has filesystem write, shell, and git-state modification inside its Docker runtime; Semantic Kernel has filesystem write and broad API/plugin access but no shell. They can still conflict over the same mutable workspace or shared files, causing overwrites or inconsistent state. Because the profiles show overlapping write surfaces but not unrestricted same-dir git writes, medium is safer than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository checkout
IF OpenHands commits or rewrites files while Semantic Kernel also mutates those files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable git writes in OpenHands for shared repos
Have Semantic Kernel write only to a staging folder

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can generate code, edits, and browser-derived outputs; Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can treat upstream outputs as plugin inputs or agent context. That makes it likely B will act on A's output without strong verification unless explicitly configured otherwise. Because downstream actions can include API calls or file writes, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel consumes OpenHands output as authoritative context
IF Semantic Kernel triggers plugins or API calls based on unverified OpenHands results
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents
Require citations or checksums for any factual claim
Route OpenHands output through a human review queue
Disable automatic action execution in Semantic Kernel

E_compliance.rationale: OpenHands handles model-provider API keys and runtime-mounted files, while Semantic Kernel handles plugin credentials and application context. If regulated or sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across different backends and logs. The profiles do not prove a specific regime breach, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in files mounted into OpenHands and also ingested into Semantic Kernel context
IF either backend retains prompts or plugin logs longer than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files
Review retention settings for both backends
Use separate API keys per agent
Document the data flow before enabling production use
